distinction_note: These are NATIVE_PDF preset configuration dependencies. The DITA-OT command-line argument dependency is the OPTIONAL preprocessing bridge inside the Native-PDF engine; it does NOT make Native PDF equivalent to the DITA_OT_PDF publishing engine (SOURCE-3). Distinction preserved.
extraction_principle: Captured as generic conditional relations (not isolated option names). Each relation records the dependency, its state branches, the coupling, and a domain-agnostic abstraction so it is reusable as reasoning evidence, never as a hardcoded option rule.

relation_types.OPTION_VISIBLE_WHEN: control is rendered/hidden based on upstream state
relation_types.OPTION_ENABLED_WHEN: control is present but active/accepted only under a condition
relation_types.OPTION_REQUIRES: control needs a prerequisite state/selection to function
relation_types.OPTION_CONTROLS_BEHAVIOR: control changes the produced output and/or the reference frame of another feature

relations.controller_state: a condition has been added/configured for the DITA map being published
state_branches: map has NO configured condition -> Condition Preset control is hidden
map HAS a configured condition -> Condition Preset control is visible and selectable
relations.coupling: authoring-time state (map conditions) gates a publish-time control's visibility
relations.evidence_verbatim: This option is visible if you have added a condition for the DITA map
relations.generic_abstraction: A consumer-of-configured-state control is VISIBLE only when the upstream authoring state it depends on exists. Coverage must include the state-absent branch (control hidden, no filtering applied) and the state-present branch (control shown, filtering applied), not just the happy path.

relations.dependent: DITA-OT command-line arguments field (e.g. -Dargs.rellinks, -Dpreprocess.* on the Native-PDF preset)
relations.controller_state: DITA-OT preprocessing is enabled for the Native-PDF preset
state_branches: DITA-OT preprocessing OFF -> command-line argument field unavailable / arguments not applied
DITA-OT preprocessing ON -> command-line argument field available and arguments passed to preprocessing
relations.coupling: a parent capability toggle enables a dependent free-text input; disabling the parent must disable/ignore the child input
relations.evidence_verbatim: DITA-OT command-line argument tokens present on the Native-PDF preset page: `-Dargs.rellinks=nofamily`, `-Dpreprocess.move-meta-entries.skip=false`
relations.evidence_status: PARTIAL — the DITA-OT argument field and example -D arguments are confirmed on the NATIVE_PDF page; the exact enabling-gate sentence ('available only when Enable DITA-OT preprocessing is selected') was supplied by the source spec but not retrieved verbatim in the sampled chunks. Verify against the Advanced tab before asserting as a hard AC.
relations.generic_abstraction: A dependent input is ENABLED/ACCEPTED only when a parent capability toggle is on. Coverage must verify: (a) child disabled/ignored when parent off, (b) child active when parent on, (c) toggling parent off after configuring the child does not silently apply stale arguments.

relations.dependent: Published content + Change-bar comparison reference frame
relations.controller_state: Baseline selection (Use Baseline / Baseline of the Previous Version)
state_branches: no baseline chosen -> current version published, change-bar reference is current/published context
Use Baseline + baseline chosen -> that baseline is published AND change-bar diffs the two selected baseline versions
relations.coupling: ONE selection changes TWO coupled outcomes: WHAT content version is published, and the REFERENCE the change-bar diff is computed against
relations.evidence_verbatim: If you select Use Baseline and choose a baseline to publish, the comparison will be done between the two selected baseline versions.
relations.generic_abstraction: A single selector changes both WHAT is produced (published version) and the REFERENCE FRAME of a derived feature (change-bar diff). The two effects are coupled: tests must assert the published version AND the diff baseline together for the same selection, never as two independent options.

relations.dependent: Change-bar output (Baseline of the Previous Version)
relations.controller_state: a current/published baseline context to diff against
state_branches: no comparison baseline available -> change bars cannot be produced
valid current + previous baseline -> change bars mark inserted/changed/deleted content
relations.coupling: the change-bar feature is meaningless without a resolvable comparison baseline; it requires the baseline selection (NPD-3) as a prerequisite
relations.evidence_verbatim: A change bar appears in the PDF to indicate the modified content ... on the left of the content that has been inserted, changed, or deleted.
relations.generic_abstraction: A derived-diff feature REQUIRES a resolvable reference. Coverage must include the missing/unresolvable-reference branch (feature no-ops or errors) and the valid-reference branch (diff rendered).

test_plan_usage: Feed these relations as state/dependency evidence to the reasoning pipeline for any NATIVE_PDF publishing ticket: each relation yields at least a controller-off and controller-on scenario branch, and NPD-3 forces a coupled published-version+diff-baseline assertion. Do NOT hardcode the option names into the skill; consume this file as run-time evidence.
